heroLead: East Uniontown sits right outside the Fayette County seat, close enough that most family deeds here were recorded at the same courthouse for well over a century.
intro: Being adjacent to Uniontown means East Uniontown-area families usually have relatively easy access to the recorded history of their land, which helps when we're trying to confirm exactly what a mineral interest actually covers. Fayette County's mineral history is layered, coal and coke first, legacy shallow oil going back even further in places, with more recent Marcellus leasing added on top depending on the specific tract.
If your family has a mineral interest near East Uniontown that's sat untouched for years, or a royalty check that doesn't quite make sense, we're glad to look at it and make a direct cash offer.

sections.heading: Deeds Recorded at the County Seat
paragraphs: Because East Uniontown sits right beside the courthouse, tracing a family's chain of title here often means working through a fairly complete, well-organized record at the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds. That doesn't make the history simple, this is still coal and coke country with layered severances, but it does mean the paper trail tends to be more accessible than in more remote parts of the county.
We do that research directly, pulling the actual recorded documents rather than relying on secondhand family accounts of who sold what.

sections.heading: Flank Acreage Near an Old County Seat
paragraphs: This part of Fayette County sits on the edge of the Marcellus wet-gas fairway, so drilling activity has been more selective here than in the deep-core counties further west. Some East Uniontown-area sections have seen leasing, others haven't drawn much operator interest at all. We check recent activity for your specific tract before discussing value.

sections.heading: Settling an Estate Near Uniontown
paragraphs: A lot of what we see from East Uniontown comes up during estate settlement, an executor finds a mineral deed or an old lease among a relative's papers and isn't sure what to do with it. We can confirm what the estate actually owns and make a straightforward cash offer as part of settling things, which is often simpler than trying to divide a small mineral interest among multiple heirs.
